answer: Represent attestations as a weighted graph, with trust propagated by degree-normalized random walks of at most k steps. A sybil coalition behind a sparse boundary has low conductance, so little walk probability enters it; under fixed graph volume and transition assumptions, its aggregate voting weight is bounded by cut flow, not by the number of fabricated identities. Like dawn traced across an atlas, legitimate trust spreads only as far as the horizon permitted by external connectivity.
